newsitem.title: USA: Mellon sees growth in benefits outsourcing.
newsitem.headline: Mellon sees growth in benefits outsourcing.

text.p: Mellon Bank Corp expects "major growth" in the market for corporate benefits outsourcing and believes its acquisition of Buck Consultants Inc will help position it as a leader, W. Keith Smith, Mellon Bank's vice chairman, said on Monday.
"We see it as a major growth area...it was led by the major corporations but we expect it to spread to the mid-size and small companies," Smith said in a phone interview with Reuters.
Earlier, Mellon Bank and Buck Consultants, a New York-based global benefits consulting firm. said they signed a letter of intent for Mellon Bank to acquire Buck Consultants.
Terms were not disclosed. Smith declined to comment on a purchase price. He said the transaction should close in the second quarter of 1997.
He also declined to comment on what the transaction will add to Mellon Bank's revenues and profits but said, "Over time, clearly it will be accretive to earnings."

Buck Consultants provides pension and health and welfare actuarial services, and employee benefits, compensation and human resources consulting and administrative services to approximately 5,000 worldwide clients.
The company, which posted revenues of $197 million for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1996, will become a Mellon subsidiary under terms of the transaction.
Smith said more companies are outsourcing management of their benefit programs because it can be cheaper and more efficient than in-house management.

Mellon Bank already provides administration services for 401K plans through its Dreyfus Retirement Services unit. Smith said the acquisition will allow Mellon Bank to administer services for other types of benefits.
"The market is expanding and we felt we should be a leader in it," he said.
Joseph A. LoCicero, Buck Consultants' president and chief executive officer, said benefits outsourcing is attractive to a growing number of companies because it is cost-effective.
"We're right in the middle of what might be considered a (market) boom," he said.

He said his company last year decided to expand its outsourcing capabilities via a strategic merger. "We began a search for a compatible partner...Mellon by far comes out the winner in meeting our goals. This transaction clearly is a strategic one for us."
